title: Functions and Parameters
summary: Write reusable functions with parameters, default values and return values.
objectives: Define a function with def and call it by name
Give a parameter a default value and override it with a keyword argument
Return a value from a function instead of printing inside it

segments.title: What you will build today
segments.body:
## What you will build today

The starter program works, but the same grade code is copied three times, once per student. When code is copy-pasted, every fix has to be made three times, and one copy always gets forgotten.

Today you will fold the three copies into **one function** called `grade_for`. It takes a mark and a pass mark, and it *returns* the word `pass` or `fail` instead of printing it. The pass mark gets a **default value** of 50, so most calls only need the mark. Then you call the function three times with different arguments and print the results.

lab.title: One grade function for every student
lab.objective: Replace three copies of the same grade code with one function that has a default parameter and a return value.
lab.instructions:
The starter program grades three students with the same code copied three times.

1. Write a function `grade_for(mark, pass_mark=50)`. Inside it, return `"pass"` when `mark` is `pass_mark` or more, otherwise return `"fail"`. The function must **return** the word, not print it.
2. Delete the three copied blocks.
3. Call the function three times and print one line per student, exactly like this:

```
Asha: pass
Ben: fail
Chen: pass
```

Asha has mark 72. Ben has mark 45. Chen has mark 45 but an easier pass mark of 40, so call `grade_for(45, pass_mark=40)` for Chen. Asha and Ben use the default pass mark, so their calls need only the mark.
lab.constraints: Name the function grade_for with parameters mark and pass_mark (default 50). Use return inside the function, not print. Print exactly three lines. No input().
lab.starter_code:
# Three copies of the SAME grade code, one per student. Your job: turn them into ONE function.

# Student 1: Asha
mark = 72
pass_mark = 50
if mark >= pass_mark:
    grade = "pass"
else:
    grade = "fail"
print("Asha: " + grade)

# Student 2: Ben
mark = 45
pass_mark = 50
if mark >= pass_mark:
    grade = "pass"
else:
    grade = "fail"
print("Ben: " + grade)

# Student 3: Chen (an easier test, so the pass mark is 40)
mark = 45
pass_mark = 40
if mark >= pass_mark:
    grade = "pass"
else:
    grade = "fail"
print("Chen: " + grade)

# 1. Above the three copies, write def grade_for(mark, pass_mark=50): that RETURNS "pass" or "fail"
# 2. Delete the three copies
# 3. Print the three lines again, this time by calling grade_for:
#    grade_for(72), grade_for(45) and grade_for(45, pass_mark=40)
hints: Start with the line def grade_for(mark, pass_mark=50): and move ONE copy of the if/else under it, indented by four spaces.
Inside the function write return "pass" in the if block and return "fail" in the else block. A return hands the word back to whoever called the function; the function itself should not print.
At the bottom, print the three lines by calling the function: print("Asha: " + grade_for(72)), print("Ben: " + grade_for(45)) and print("Chen: " + grade_for(45, pass_mark=40)).

visible_examples.description: A default parameter and a keyword argument
visible_examples.code:
def greeting(name, word="Hello"):
    return word + ", " + name + "!"

print(greeting("Asha"))
print(greeting("Ben", word="Hi"))

visible_examples.description: A function that returns one of two words

success_criteria: grade_for(72) returns pass (the default pass mark of 50 is used)
Your program prints exactly the three student lines

tests.label: grade_for is a function
tests.remediation: Define the function with def grade_for(mark, pass_mark=50): above the place where you call it.

tests.label: grade_for(72) returns pass
tests.remediation: Give pass_mark a default of 50 in the def line, and use return "pass" when mark >= pass_mark.
tests.objective: Use a default parameter value and return a value

tests.label: grade_for(45, pass_mark=40) returns pass
tests.remediation: Compare mark with the pass_mark parameter, not with the number 50, so a different pass mark changes the answer.
tests.objective: Override a default with a keyword argument

tests.label: grade_for(45) returns fail
tests.remediation: The function must return "fail" when the mark is below the pass mark. Check the else branch returns "fail".
tests.objective: Return a value from a function

tests.label: Your program prints exactly the three student lines
tests.remediation: Print exactly three lines: Asha: pass, Ben: fail, Chen: pass. The function should only return the word; print it where you call the function, not inside the function.
tests.objective: Call a function with different arguments

lab.solution:
def grade_for(mark, pass_mark=50):
    if mark >= pass_mark:
        return "pass"
    return "fail"


print("Asha: " + grade_for(72))
print("Ben: " + grade_for(45))
print("Chen: " + grade_for(45, pass_mark=40))
